title: Smart Ops Attach Proxy with signal-highlighting and runbook templates
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: During high-severity incidents we frequently receive PD alerts and Slack escalations that lack consistent telemetry artifacts (trace anchors, prefiltered log snippets, and summarized metric windows). On-call rotation spends time manually hunting for the right traces and building runbook links. Goal: provide a lightweight proxy that enriches PagerDuty and Slack incident payloads with curated telemetry attachments, highlights probable signal spans, and auto-inserts templated runbook sections to speed TTR and improve postmortem fidelity.

Scope: build an 'attach-proxy' service that sits between our alerting hooks and downstream PD/Slack integrations. It will: 1) run quick signal extraction (span sampling, anomaly metric window, top-k log lines); 2) attach compact artifacts to PD incidents and Slack threads; 3) embed a small runbook template populated with incident metadata and suggested remediation steps; 4) surface a link to a trace-focused debug UI; 5) record which attachments were added for postmortem automation and SLO analysis.
acceptance_criteria:
1) PagerDuty incidents created via our API include a 3-part telemetry attachment: a) span anchor link + top 5 spans, b) metric snapshot (last 5m vs baseline), c) top-10 log excerpts with context.
2) Slack channel alerts include the same compact attachments and a one-click 'Open runbook' link that preloads an editable runbook draft.
3) Attach-proxy exposes a small audit endpoint (internal) listing attachments per incident ID.
4) Integration tests that simulate high-volume alerts validate that attachment creation adds <200ms median overhead to webhook processing and <2s p99.
5) Postmortem automation pipeline can consume the attachment audit records to auto-populate a postmortem draft with linked telemetry references.
tasks: Design attach-proxy API and message schema (trace anchors, metric snapshot format, log excerpt schema)
Prototype fast signal extractor (Go) using existing trace sampling library and metric query cache
Implement Slack block builder with compact telemetry attachments and runbook template insertion
Implement PD webhook enrichment flow with attachment upload and incident note insertion
Add audit table and internal GET endpoint for attachments (for postmortem automation)
Load test the enrichment path to validate latency and resource cost
Create integration tests and end-to-end demo script
Document runbook templates and update on-call playbooks
notes:
Design doc: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/OBS/pages/Smart+Ops+Attach+Proxy. Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/487. Runbook templates in Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-RunbookTemplates. Debug UI ticket: PM-6142 (links to trace debugger).

Implementation decisions so far:
- We'll keep the proxy stateless for scale; attachments metadata written to a small DynamoDB table for auditing.
- Use existing metric-store read replica for quick 1min-window queries; pre-warm cache for common alert queries.
- Start with a conservative attachment size cap (2000 chars for log excerpts + compressed trace anchor) to avoid PD/Slack rate limits.
- Runbook templates will be Markdown with parameter tokens: incident_id, service, top_span, suggested_rollbacks.

Open questions:
- Should we encrypt attachments at-rest with customer KMS for enterprise incidents? (security review pending)
- PD attachment size strategy for very large trace contexts — fall back to hosted trace link only?
